tagline: North out of Kayenta until the monuments stand up ahead.
intro: US 163 leaves Kayenta as a five-lane street and narrows to two lanes on the way north, about 5,500 feet up on a flat, stark desert floor from which the rock rises abruptly. Past Owl Rock the grassland gives way to pinyon and juniper, and as the road nears the Utah line the buttes and spires of Monument Valley come into view.
Many of the pullouts along the way were made by drivers stopping to photograph the rocks, or to look over a jewelry stand. All of it is Navajo Nation land.

moments.title: Kayenta
moments.text: Its Navajo name means fingers of water, for the way rain runs down the local rock. It is the only township under Navajo law.

moments.title: Agathla Peak
moments.text: A volcanic plug rising 1,500 feet, seven miles north of town. The name means much wool, for the antelope and deer fur that collects on the rock.

moments.title: Goulding's
moments.text: Just over the Utah line, a 1928 trading post whose owner sent photographs of the valley to John Ford. Ford came and shot Stagecoach, and several more westerns after it.
